cards.title: The 20-second handwashing technique with soap and water
facts: Washing hands with soap for 20 seconds breaks down viral lipid envelopes and rinses off pathogenic bacteria.
Soap requires friction across all surfaces (palms, back of hands, between fingers, thumbs, and fingernails).
do: Wet hands with clean water, apply soap, and lather vigorously for at least 20 full seconds (hum 'Happy Birthday' twice)
Scrub all zones: palm to palm, backs of hands, interlaced fingers, thumbs, and fingertips into palms
Rinse thoroughly under running water and dry with a clean personal towel
dont: Never just splash water for 2 seconds without soap and call it 'clean'
Never wipe clean hands on dirty pants or unwashed shirts

myths.statement: Splashing hands with plain tap water for 3 seconds removes all germs effectively.
myths.truth: Plain water cannot break down greasy dirt or viral membranes. Soap friction for 20 seconds is essential.

quiz.q: How long should you rub your hands with soap to ensure complete bacterial and viral removal?
quiz.explanation: 20 seconds of soap friction physically destroys viral membranes and lifts microbial dirt.

situations: Before eating lunch at {at}, {name} rushes to the washroom sink to clean hands.
scenario.question: How should {name} execute proper hand hygiene?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Apply soap and scrub vigorously for 20 seconds across palms, backs, fingers, and nails
rubric.note: Covers all anatomical hand surfaces thoroughly.

rubric.point: Rinse thoroughly under running water to flush away loosened dirt and microbes
rubric.note: Flushes dislodged germs down the drain.

rubric.point: Dry hands with a clean dry towel rather than wiping on school uniform

sources.name: WHO Guidelines on Hand Hygiene in Health Care and Schools

cards.title: Dental health: Brushing twice daily and tongue cleaning
facts: Mouth bacteria feed on residual food sugars, producing lactic acid that dissolves protective tooth enamel (cavities).
Brushing before bed removes overnight plaque acids when saliva flow drops during sleep.
do: Brush teeth twice daily: once in the morning and once at night before going to bed for 2 full minutes
Use gentle circular strokes along the gumline with a soft-bristled toothbrush; clean tongue with a tongue cleaner
Rinse your mouth with clean water after eating sweet, sticky, or starchy foods
dont: Never scrub teeth horizontally like a saw with hard bristles (erodes protective enamel and gums)
Never go to sleep with sweet chocolate or candy coating your teeth

myths.statement: Brushing your teeth violently hard with a stiff brush cleans them twice as well.
myths.truth: Hard brushing erodes protective tooth enamel and causes painful receding gum tissue. Use gentle circular motions.

quiz.q: Why is brushing your teeth at night before bed even more critical than morning brushing?
options: Saliva production drops during sleep, allowing trapped sugar acids to destroy enamel undisturbed all night
quiz.explanation: Night brushing removes food substrates before nocturnal dry mouth allows bacterial acid attacks.

situations: Getting ready for bed at {at}, {name} considers skipping nighttime tooth brushing because of tiredness.
scenario.question: What dental habit should {name} uphold?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Spend 2 minutes gently brushing teeth with circular strokes before sleeping
rubric.note: Removes sugar plaque before nighttime bacterial acid attacks.
rubric.keys: brush teeth at night|2 minutes|soft brush|circular strokes

rubric.point: Clean the tongue gently to remove bacterial coating and freshen breath
rubric.note: Reduces oral microbial load and bad breath.

rubric.point: Rinse with water and smile with clean, protected teeth

dangerous: scrub teeth violently with wire brush

cards.title: Daily bathing, fresh undergarments and hygiene in humid weather
facts: Warm, humid climates encourage fungal skin infections (ringworm, athlete's foot) in sweaty skin folds.
Sweat itself is odorless; body odor is caused by skin bacteria fermenting apocrine sweat secretions.
do: Bathe daily with water and soap, paying special attention to armpits, groin, neck, and feet
Change into clean, fresh undergarments and breathable cotton clothes every single day
Dry skin folds thoroughly with a clean towel before putting on fresh clothes
dont: Never re-wear damp, sweaty unwashed undergarments or socks from yesterday
Never leave damp towels rolled up in a dark corner (breeds mold and mildew)

myths.statement: Spray perfume or deodorant heavily over unwashed sweaty clothes replaces the need for a daily bath.
myths.truth: Perfume mixed with stale sweat creates an intensely unpleasant odor and fails to remove skin bacteria.

quiz.q: What type of clothing fabric is healthiest for hot, humid Indian weather?
quiz.explanation: Cotton absorbs sweat and allows cross-ventilation, preventing fungal skin infections.

situations: After an active, sweaty sports session at {at}, {name} prepares to change clothes.
scenario.question: What personal hygiene routine keeps skin healthy and fresh?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Take a refreshing bath with soap and water to wash away sweat and bacteria
rubric.note: Cleanses skin pores and prevents fungal infections.

rubric.point: Dry skin thoroughly and change into fresh, clean cotton undergarments
rubric.note: Keeps skin dry and prevents chafing.

rubric.point: Hang up used damp clothes and towel in sunlight or airy place to dry
rubric.note: Prevents bacterial and fungal growth on textiles.

dangerous: wear sweaty clothes 3 days in a row

sources.name: Indian Association of Dermatologists (IADVL Public Education)

cards.title: Nail hygiene: Trimming straight, clean fingernails and no biting
facts: The dark crevice beneath long fingernails harbors thousands of fecal bacteria, pinworm eggs, and viruses.
Biting nails transfers infectious pathogens directly into the mouth and causes painful nail bed infections (paronychia).
do: Trim fingernails and toenails regularly using a clean nail clipper, cutting straight across
Scrub gently under fingernails with soap and water while washing hands
Keep nails neatly trimmed and smooth with an emery board or file
dont: Never bite or chew fingernails or peel off ragged cuticle skin with teeth
Never share unsterilized nail clippers with people who have fungal nail infections

myths.statement: Biting your fingernails is a harmless nervous habit that doesn't affect your health.
myths.truth: Nail biting ingests pinworm eggs, causes oral dental misalignment, and leads to severe bacterial finger infections.

quiz.q: Why is keeping fingernails short and clean vital before eating food with your hands in India?
options: Long nails harbor dangerous bacteria and worm eggs that contaminate food eaten with hands
quiz.explanation: Eating with short, clean nails prevents accidental ingestion of trapped bacterial dirt.

situations: Examining their hands at {at}, {name} notices long fingernails with dark dirt trapped underneath.
scenario.question: How should {name} practice proper nail hygiene?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Trim fingernails neatly using a clean nail clipper, cutting smoothly straight across
rubric.note: Removes the primary trap for microbial contamination.
rubric.keys: trim nails|clean nail clipper|cut straight across

rubric.point: Scrub gently under nails with soap and a soft brush while washing hands
Avoid biting nails or tearing cuticles with teeth

cards.title: Respiratory etiquette: The elbow crook cough and tissue disposal
facts: A single sneeze launches over 40,000 microscopic droplets at speeds up to 160 km/h.
Coughing into bare palms transfers infectious viruses onto door handles, shared pencils, and bus rails.
do: Cough or sneeze into the crook of your elbow ('the Dracula cough') if no tissue is available
Use a clean paper tissue to cover your nose and mouth when sneezing, and discard in a closed dustbin
Wash hands immediately with soap and water or use sanitizer after blowing your nose
dont: Never cough or sneeze openly into classroom air without covering
Never cough directly into bare palms that touch doorknobs and friends' hands

myths.statement: Coughing into your bare hands is the polite, standard way to cover your mouth.
myths.truth: Hands touch desks, food, and doorknobs, rapidly spreading flu and colds to everyone. Cough into your elbow crook.

quiz.q: Why is sneezing into your elbow crook vastly superior to sneezing into your bare hand?
options: Your inner elbow rarely touches shared objects like doorknobs, stopping the spread of germs
quiz.explanation: The elbow crook contains droplets without contaminating hands that touch shared surfaces.

situations: In a crowded classroom at {at}, {name} feels a sudden, powerful sneeze coming on.
scenario.question: What is the hygienic respiratory response?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Raise your inner elbow crook to cover your mouth and nose tightly as you sneeze
rubric.note: Blocks respiratory droplets from contaminating hands or air.
rubric.keys: elbow crook|sneeze in elbow|cover with elbow

rubric.point: Or use a clean paper tissue and discard it immediately into a waste bin
Wash hands with soap afterwards if hands touched any nasal fluids

dangerous: sneeze into bare palms then touch doorknob

sources.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Respiratory Hygiene)

cards.title: Head lice facts: Gentle treatment, no sharing combs and zero shame
facts: Head lice are tiny wingless insects that crawl; they CANNOT jump, fly, or transmit any diseases.
Lice infestation has zero connection to personal cleanliness; anyone can catch lice through direct head-to-head contact.
do: Tell parents calmly if your scalp feels intensely itchy, especially behind ears or at the nape of the neck
Use a fine-toothed anti-lice comb and gentle medicated anti-lice shampoo recommended by a doctor
Wash bedsheets, pillowcases, and hats in warm water to prevent re-infestation
dont: Never tease or shame a classmate who has head lice (it has nothing to do with cleanliness)
Never share personal hair combs, brushes, caps, or helmets with others

myths.statement: Having head lice means a child is dirty and never washes their hair.
myths.truth: Lice actually prefer clean, healthy hair. Head lice is a common, easily treatable childhood occurrence with zero shame.

quiz.q: How do head lice actually travel from one child's hair to another?
options: They crawl through direct head-to-head contact or sharing personal caps and combs
quiz.explanation: Lice have claws for crawling along hair shafts; they cannot jump or fly.

situations: A classmate at {at} is embarrassed because their scalp is itchy and has head lice.
scenario.question: How should {name} respond with kindness and scientific clarity?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Reassure the classmate that head lice is very common, easily treated, and NOT caused by being dirty
Advise consulting parents for a gentle medicated shampoo and fine-toothed nit comb
Avoid head-to-head contact and do not share personal combs, caps, or hairbands

cards.title: School washroom etiquette: Flushing, cleanliness and washing hands
facts: Unhygienic public washrooms spread urinary tract infections (UTIs) and gastrointestinal bugs.
Leaving a washroom clean for the next user is a fundamental civic and hygienic responsibility.
do: Always flush the toilet completely after every use, holding the flush handle until clean water cycles
Dispose of sanitary pads, tissues, and trash in designated dustbins, NEVER into the toilet bowl (causes choking)
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after every single washroom visit
dont: Never stand or squat on Western ceramic toilet seats with dirty shoes (causes catastrophic toilet bowl shattering)
Never leave toilet seats wet or un-flushed

myths.statement: Flushing the toilet is unnecessary if you only used it for a short time.
myths.truth: Leaving unflushed waste breeds foul ammonia odors and attracts flies that transmit gastrointestinal bacteria.

quiz.q: Where should used paper towels and sanitary pads always be disposed of in a school washroom?
options: In the dedicated covered sanitary waste dustbin
quiz.explanation: Flushing pads or thick paper chokes sewer plumbing. Always use the dustbin.

situations: Using the school or public washroom at {at}, {name} finishes and prepares to leave.
scenario.question: What complete hygiene and civic routine should {name} execute?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Flush the toilet completely and ensure the bowl is spotless for the next person
Dispose of all tissues or waste into the closed dustbin, not the flush
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before returning to class

dangerous: stand on western seat with muddy shoes

cards.title: Sun protection in tropical heat: Shade, cotton and hydration
facts: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation is strongest between 11 AM and 3 PM, causing painful sunburns and cellular damage.
Wearing wide-brim hats, sunglasses, and breathable clothing shields delicate facial skin naturally.
do: Seek shade under trees or covered verandahs during intense peak midday sun hours
Wear a cap or carry an umbrella when walking outside in bright tropical sunlight
Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen (SPF 30+) on exposed face, neck, and arms before prolonged outdoor sports
dont: Never stare directly at the sun (causes irreversible solar retinal burns and blindness)
Never stay outdoors without drinking water during high UV index days

myths.statement: You only need sun protection on hot sunny days; cloudy days have zero harmful UV radiation.
myths.truth: Up to 80% of solar UV rays penetrate cloud cover. Sun protection matters whenever the UV index is moderate to high.

quiz.q: What is the most effective natural way to protect your face and neck from scorching afternoon sun?
options: Wearing a wide-brim hat or cap and staying in shaded areas
quiz.explanation: Hats, umbrellas, and natural shade block direct UV photons from damaging skin tissue.

situations: Spending sports day outdoors under bright scorching sunlight at {at}, {name}'s skin begins feeling hot and red.
scenario.question: How should {name} protect their skin and health?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Seek shade under canopies or trees whenever not actively competing on the field
Wear a cap or hat and apply sunscreen to exposed neck and face
Drink water regularly to keep skin and body hydrated from within

dangerous: stay in sun without water for 6 hours

sources.name: Indian Association of Dermatologists Sun Safety Guidelines

cards.title: Ear hygiene: Nothing smaller than your elbow in your ear
facts: Earwax (cerumen) is a healthy, protective substance that traps dust, bacteria, and insects naturally.
Ears are self-cleaning organs; inserting cotton buds or hairpin objects pushes wax deep against the eardrum.
do: Remember the golden ENT medical rule: 'Never put anything smaller than your elbow inside your ear'
Clean only the external outer ear (pinna) with a soft towel after bathing
Consult an ENT doctor if your ear feels blocked, painful, or has yellowish discharge
dont: Never insert cotton ear buds, safety pins, matchsticks, or car keys into your ear canal
Never pour unverified warm oil or herbal concoctions into ears without medical advice

myths.statement: Cotton ear buds are designed to be shoved deep inside your ear canal to dig out wax.
myths.truth: Cotton buds pack wax into hard impactions against the eardrum and risk perforating delicate ear membranes.

quiz.q: What does earwax actually do inside your ear canal?
options: It is a protective natural barrier with antimicrobial properties that traps dust and insects
quiz.explanation: Earwax lubricates the ear canal and possesses natural antibacterial enzymes.

situations: After taking a bath at {at}, {name}'s friend takes a safety pin or cotton bud to dig inside their ear.
scenario.question: What urgent ENT safety advice should {name} deliver?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stop them immediately: 'Never insert cotton buds, pins, or keys into your ear canal'
rubric.note: Prevents eardrum perforation and hearing trauma.
rubric.keys: never put buds in ear|no pins in ear|eardrum danger

rubric.point: Explain that earwax is natural protection and the ear canal cleans itself outward automatically
rubric.keys: ear cleans itself|earwax is protective|wax pushes outward

rubric.point: Advise wiping only the outer ear with a clean towel and seeing a doctor if blocked
rubric.keys: wipe outer ear|see doctor if blocked

dangerous: pour hot mustard oil in ear

sources.name: Association of Otolaryngologists of India (AOI Ear Care)

cards.title: Personal hygiene boundaries: Never sharing towels, bottles and razors
facts: Damp towels and washcloths harbor fungi, staphylococcus bacteria, and scabies mites.
Directly sharing drinking bottles mouth-to-mouth transmits glandular fever, throat infections, and cold sores.
do: Use your own personal towel, toothbrush, hairbrush, and drinking water bottle
If sharing water with a friend, pour water into their mouth from above without touching bottle lips ('fountain drinking')
Wash your bath towel and pillowcase weekly in warm soapy water and dry thoroughly in sunlight
dont: Never share toothbrushes (transmits bloodborne bacteria through micro-gum bleeds)
Never use an unfamiliar person's shaving razor, nail clipper, or unwashed towel

myths.statement: Sharing your personal toothbrush with your best friend is a great sign of close friendship.
myths.truth: Sharing toothbrushes transfers oral pathogens and bloodborne viruses directly into gum micro-abrasions.

quiz.q: Why must you never share personal items like toothbrushes, razors, or wet towels?
options: They transfer infectious skin bacteria, bloodborne viruses, and fungal spores between bodies
quiz.explanation: Personal hygiene items contact body fluids and broken skin, transferring pathogens directly.

situations: At school or sports practice at {at}, a classmate asks to share {name}'s personal towel and drink from their bottle.
scenario.question: How can {name} share water safely while maintaining hygiene boundaries?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Pour water from above into their mouth without letting their lips touch the bottle rim
rubric.note: Prevents saliva and oral pathogen cross-contamination.
rubric.keys: pour from above|no lip contact|hygienic water sharing

rubric.point: Politely explain that personal bath towels and toothbrushes should never be shared
Wash and sanitize your personal water bottle and towel regularly at home

dangerous: wipe face with friend's sweaty towel
share lip balm mouth to mouth

cards.title: Mosquito defense: Dengue, malaria and eliminating stagnant water
facts: Aedes mosquitoes (which transmit Dengue and Chikungunya) bite primarily during early morning and late afternoon.
Aedes mosquitoes breed in clean, stagnant water inside household flowerpots, air coolers, and discarded plastic cups.
do: Inspect and empty all stagnant water from air coolers, flowerpot saucers, and terrace tins once every week ('Dry Day')
Wear light-colored, full-sleeve shirts and full pants when playing outdoors in the evening
Use mosquito nets while sleeping and apply safe natural mosquito repellent lotion
dont: Never allow stagnant water to pool in open drums, old tires, or rooftop overhead tanks
Never ignore high sudden fever accompanied by severe pain behind the eyes (dengue danger)

myths.statement: Dengue mosquitoes breed in dirty sewer gutters and only bite in the middle of midnight darkness.
myths.truth: Aedes dengue mosquitoes breed in CLEAN, fresh stagnant water (coolers, flower vases) and bite during daytime hours.

quiz.q: Where do dengue-carrying Aedes mosquitoes commonly breed in urban homes?
options: In clean, undisturbed stagnant water in air coolers, flowerpot saucers, and discarded coconut shells
quiz.explanation: Aedes lays eggs on the waterline of clean stagnant containers; weekly emptying stops the life cycle.

situations: Observing home surroundings at {at}, {name} notices stagnant water sitting in flowerpot plates and an old cooler.
scenario.question: What mosquito control action should {name} take?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Empty and scrub clean all flowerpot saucers, bird baths, and cooler trays immediately
rubric.note: Destroys mosquito larvae breeding sites completely.
rubric.keys: empty stagnant water|clean cooler|dry day|flowerpot saucers

rubric.point: Wear full-sleeve clothing and apply mosquito repellent during morning and evening hours
Ensure overhead water tanks are securely covered with tight-fitting lids
rubric.note: Blocks mosquito entry to water reserves.

sources.name: National Center for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC)

cards.title: Sick day care: Resting, staying home and returning safely
facts: Attending school with an active contagious viral fever spreads infection to dozens of classmates.
Rest, hydration, and fever monitoring allow your body's immune system to clear infections efficiently.
do: Stay home from school if you have a fever (above 37.8°C / 100°F), vomiting, or contagious rash
Rest in bed, drink plenty of fluids (water, soups, ORS, fresh fruit juices), and eat light meals
Return to school only after being fever-free for at least 24 hours without taking fever-reducing medicines
dont: Never force yourself to attend school exams with high burning fever
Never self-medicate with leftover prescription antibiotics for common viral colds

myths.statement: Going to school with high fever proves you are a heroic, dedicated student.
myths.truth: Attending school while sick spreads contagion to peers, delays your own recovery, and risks medical collapse.

quiz.q: When is it safe to return to school after recovering from a contagious fever?
options: At least 24 hours after your fever has completely resolved without fever-reducing pills
quiz.explanation: The 24-hour fever-free milestone ensures viral shedding has dropped to safe non-contagious levels.

situations: Waking up with high fever, sore throat, and shivering body at {at}, {name} has a school test.
scenario.question: What is the responsible health decision?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Stay home, inform the school, and focus on rest, hydration, and medical recovery
rubric.note: Protects personal health and stops schoolwide viral spread.

rubric.point: Drink plenty of warm liquids, soups, and consult a doctor with parents
Return to school only after being completely fever-free for at least 24 hours

dangerous: go to school with high fever

sources.name: Indian Academy of Pediatrics School Health Guidelines

cards.title: Growing up: Normal physical and emotional changes of puberty
facts: Puberty is the natural biological transition from childhood to young adulthood triggered by hormones.
Everyone's puberty timeline is completely unique; starting earlier or later than peers is 100% normal.
do: Understand that bodily changes (growth spurts, voice deepening, body hair, sweat increase) are natural and healthy
Maintain daily bathing, wear clean cotton clothes, and talk openly with trusted parents, doctors, or counselors
Treat your own developing body and your classmates' changes with dignity, kindness, and zero teasing
dont: Never feel ashamed, scared, or embarrassed about natural biological development
Never mock or tease classmates whose voices crack or who experience rapid growth spurts

myths.statement: If your voice cracks or you grow taller later than your friends, there is something medically wrong with you.
myths.truth: Every human body has an individual biological clock. Puberty variation across ages 10 to 16 is entirely normal.

quiz.q: What biological chemical messengers trigger growth spurts and body changes during puberty?
options: Natural hormones (like testosterone and estrogen) released by the endocrine system
quiz.explanation: Hormones orchestrate natural adolescent growth spurts, bone density increase, and maturity.

situations: Experiencing sudden growth spurts, voice changes, or oily skin at {at}, {name} feels confused and self-conscious.
scenario.question: What reassuring scientific understanding should {name} remember?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize that puberty changes are natural, healthy biological milestones of growing up
rubric.keys: natural changes|puberty is normal|healthy milestones|growing up

rubric.point: Talk openly with trusted parents, school nurse, or counselor about any questions
Maintain daily hygiene with gentle bathing and treat developing bodies with respect

sources.name: Adolescent Health Division (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare - RKSK)

cards.title: Menstrual hygiene fundamentals: Normal biology and clean care
facts: Menstruation is a completely natural, healthy biological process showing that the reproductive system is functional.
Good menstrual hygiene prevents reproductive tract infections and enables girls to study and play with confidence.
do: Change sanitary pads every 4 to 6 hours (or clean menstrual cups/reusable cloth pads hygienically)
Wrap used sanitary pads neatly in newspaper and dispose of them in a covered dustbin (NEVER flush in toilets)
Maintain daily bathing with clean water and wear clean, dry, breathable cotton underwear
dont: Never flush sanitary pads down the toilet (causes catastrophic plumbing blockages)
Never treat menstruation as 'impure', dirty, or a topic of shame or stigma

myths.statement: A girl on her period is impure and must sit isolated in a dark corner without touching food.
myths.truth: Menstruation is a pure, clean, natural biological cycle. Ancient taboos and isolation myths have zero scientific validity.

quiz.q: How often should a sanitary pad be changed to maintain optimal hygiene and prevent bacterial growth?
options: Every 4 to 6 hours (or sooner if heavily soaked)
quiz.explanation: Changing pads every 4-6 hours prevents bacterial multiplication and skin rash.

situations: A student in Class 7 at {at} experiences her period at school for the first time and feels panicked.
scenario.question: How should {name} and friends respond with compassionate, dignified care?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Reassure her that periods are completely natural, normal, and nothing to feel scared or ashamed of
rubric.note: Provides immediate emotional comfort and destigmatization.

rubric.point: Help her visit the school nurse or female teacher to obtain a clean sanitary pad
rubric.note: Facilitates access to menstrual hygiene products.

rubric.point: Wrap used pads in paper and dispose of them in the covered washroom dustbin

cards.title: Understanding body odour: Sweat glands, daily washing and clean fabrics
facts: During puberty, apocrine sweat glands develop in armpits and groin, producing protein-rich sweat.
Bacteria naturally living on skin break down this sweat, which creates body odour (BO).
do: Wash armpits and body thoroughly with soap and warm water during your daily bath
Wear freshly washed, clean cotton clothes every day—never re-wear sweaty yesterday shirts
Use an antiperspirant or gentle deodorant on clean, dry skin after bathing if desired
dont: Never mask body odour with heavy sprays of perfume instead of taking a bath
Never shame or bully classmates about body odour; offer gentle, private advice if asked

myths.statement: Sweat itself smells naturally disgusting the instant it comes out of your pores.
myths.truth: Fresh sweat is 100% odorless. Odour only develops hours later when surface skin bacteria ferment the sweat.

quiz.q: What actually causes body odour in armpits during puberty?
options: Skin bacteria breaking down sweat secreted by apocrine glands
quiz.explanation: Bacterial breakdown of organic sweat components produces characteristic body odor.

situations: After gym class at {at}, {name} notices body odour and feels conscious about teammates.
scenario.question: What is the effective, scientific personal care solution?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Take a daily bath using soap and water, washing armpits and skin folds thoroughly
rubric.note: Cleanses away the bacteria that cause body odour.
rubric.keys: daily bath|soap and water|wash armpits|body hygiene

rubric.point: Wear clean, freshly laundered cotton clothes every day
rubric.note: Prevents wearing stale bacterial sweat residue.

rubric.point: Use a mild deodorant on clean dry skin rather than spraying heavily over dirty sweat

dangerous: spray whole bottle perfume over sweat

sources.name: Indian Association of Dermatologists (Adolescent Skin Care)

cards.title: Sanitizing school water bottles, straws and tiffin box gaskets
facts: Moist rubber gaskets inside tiffin boxes and silicone bottle straws harbor invisible black mold and biofilm.
Drinking from moldy water bottles causes persistent throat irritation, stomach cramps, and diarrhea.
do: Wash your school water bottle daily with hot water, liquid soap, and a bottle brush
Remove rubber sealing rings and silicone straws from tiffin lids weekly to scrub away hidden black mold
Allow water bottles and tiffins to air-dry completely upside down on a dish rack before closing lids
dont: Never leave water sitting in school bottles for 5 days over the weekend
Never leave leftover food rotting inside closed tiffin boxes in your school bag

myths.statement: Rinsing your water bottle with plain cold water once a month is enough to keep it clean.
myths.truth: Saliva backwash and moisture create thick slimy bacterial biofilms inside bottles that only soap scrubbing removes.

quiz.q: Where does dangerous black mold secretly grow inside school tiffin boxes and sipper bottles?
options: Inside the silicone rubber lid gaskets and straw crevices
quiz.explanation: Silicone sealing gaskets trap moisture and food grease, forming toxic mold colonies if unwashed.

situations: Opening a school water bottle at {at}, {name} notices a black slimy ring around the rubber lid gasket.
scenario.question: How should {name} sanitize this container properly?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Remove the rubber gasket and scrub it thoroughly with hot water, soap, and an old brush
rubric.note: Removes hazardous fungal mold colonies completely.
rubric.keys: remove gasket|scrub with soap|hot water|bottle brush

rubric.point: Wash the bottle inside out with bottle brush and let it air-dry completely
rubric.note: Ensures complete drying so mold cannot regrow.

rubric.point: Commit to washing school drinking bottles with soap daily after returning home

sources.name: FSSAI Clean Food and Water Storage Norms

cards.title: Foot hygiene: Washing feet, changing socks and airing sports shoes
facts: Feet have over 250,000 sweat glands; closed canvas school shoes create dark, warm, humid incubators.
Athlete's foot is a common fungal infection causing intense itching and peeling between toes.
do: Wash feet thoroughly with soap and water every day, especially scrubbing between all toes
Dry your feet completely with a towel before putting on socks and shoes (fungi love moisture)
Wear clean, fresh cotton socks every day and air out your sports shoes in sunlight or breezy balconies
dont: Never wear the same sweaty, damp socks two days in a row
Never wear damp sports shoes that have not dried out from yesterday's rain

myths.statement: Smelly shoes are caused by bad luck and have nothing to do with washing feet or socks.
myths.truth: Smelly feet (bromodosis) are caused by bacteria fermenting trapped foot sweat in unwashed socks.

quiz.q: What simple daily habit eliminates smelly feet and prevents athlete's foot fungus?
options: Washing feet with soap, drying thoroughly between toes, and wearing fresh clean cotton socks daily
quiz.explanation: Clean socks and dry inter-toe skin eliminate the humid breeding ground for foot bacteria and fungi.

situations: Taking off sports shoes after school at {at}, {name}'s shoes smell intensely and toes feel damp and itchy.
scenario.question: What foot hygiene routine restores comfort?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Wash feet immediately with soap and water, scrubbing and drying thoroughly between toes
rubric.keys: wash feet with soap|dry between toes|clean feet

rubric.point: Put damp socks in the laundry and wear a fresh, clean pair of cotton socks tomorrow
rubric.keys: fresh socks daily|clean cotton socks|wash socks

rubric.point: Loosen shoelaces and leave sports shoes outside in an airy, sunny spot to dry out completely
rubric.note: Solar UV and air circulation eliminate damp shoe odors.

dangerous: wear same sweaty socks all week
keep wet shoes inside closed cupboard

cards.title: Teen skin care fundamentals: Gentle washing, water and no fairness fads
facts: Adolescent hormones stimulate sebaceous glands, producing excess sebum that clogs pores into pimples (acne).
Squeezing or popping pimples pushes bacteria deeper into the dermis, causing permanent pitted scars.
do: Wash your face twice daily with plain water or a mild, gentle soap-free cleanser
Drink plenty of water and eat fruits and vegetables to keep skin healthy from within
Consult a certified dermatologist if acne is painful or persistent—treatments exist!
dont: Never squeeze, pop, or scratch acne pimples with fingernails (leaves permanent scars)
Never use harsh chemical fairness bleaching creams (many contain toxic steroids and mercury)

myths.statement: Skin fairness bleaching creams are safe everyday cosmetics that make you successful in life.
myths.truth: Fairness creams often contain dangerous steroids that permanently thin skin and damage health. Embrace your natural skin tone with pride.

quiz.q: Why must you NEVER squeeze or pop a pimple on your face?
options: Popping pushes infection deeper into skin tissues, leading to inflammation and permanent scarring
quiz.explanation: Popping breaks the follicular wall, spreading infection and leaving permanent pitted hyperpigmentation.
